# F6 · Refresh and regeneration

*Extracted verbatim from the PRD, which remains the single source of truth for every criterion below. Edit the PRD, then regenerate — never edit this file.*

Identifiers in this file: `F6-AC-01` – `F6-UP-04`.

#### F6 · Refresh and regeneration

| Section | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Priority | **Must.** The second of only two named customer jobs in 2.3 — without it, safely re-running advice doesn't exist as a feature at all. |
| Serves | The second core job in Section 2.3: re-decide safely when the world moves. |
| Happy path | The world moves — injuries, price changes, announced lineups — and the manager re-runs the advice without losing the decisions already made. Governing principle: his decisions are locks; everything unlocked is regenerated. |
| **How a Refresh Re-Scores a Call** |  |
| **F6-RS-01** | The prior recommendation and the judgement inputs behind it are carried forward as the baseline. A refresh revises them; it does not start again. |
| **F6-RS-02** | **Code diffs the evidence first, across every player FPL tracks — not only the players already inside an existing call.** The diff is mechanical and free, and runs against every field FPL's own feed carries per player, compared with what was on file at the last successful run: the status code (available / injured / suspended / left the league / doubtful), the free-text `news` line and its timestamp, the chance-of-playing figure, and price. FPL already uses status and news to capture the "thousand other things" — sold, loaned out, retired, suspended — so diffing the whole record catches them without naming each one. |
| **F6-RS-03** | A new item published by the team-news sources (Premier Fantasy Tools, Premier Injuries) since the last successful run counts as evidence too. |
| **F6-RS-04** | Any change in any of those counts as new evidence; none needs a magnitude threshold. Elapsed time alone is never a trigger — refresh is manual, so nothing changing while time passes is a legitimate nothing-changed outcome. |
| **F6-RS-05** | **A player who was never proposed is diffed the same way as one already in a call, and can surface as a brand-new candidate.** A player whose injury kept him off the table has no existing call to diff against, but his record is still tracked and still compared; if his status improves enough to make him viable — a doubt clearing, a suspension ending — that is new evidence like any other, the model is called, and the candidate-proposal step (3.2, engine step 1) reads the whole world fresh. This is what makes "pending calls are discarded and rewritten freely" mean what it says. |
| **F6-RS-06** | **A squad correction (F2) is new evidence too, and runs the same regeneration rather than a separate one.** |
| **F6-RS-07** | **Only a squad correction can contradict a lock outright.** Where the screenshot shows something other than what a selected call expected, the screenshot wins, because it is what is true: the contradicted lock is broken and dropped rather than force-kept, and is reported through the same refresh diff ("call X was based on a squad state that has changed and no longer applies") rather than silently vanishing. |
| **F6-RS-08** | **If no new evidence has landed, the model is not called at all.** The stored judgement is reused and the conviction figure is identical. Most refreshes should cost nothing. |
| **F6-RS-09** | **If new evidence has landed, the model is called with both the prior judgement and the new fact**, and asked to re-rate. Anchoring it to its own previous answer stops the figure wandering on nothing while still letting real news move it. |
| **F6-RS-10** | **The model is never asked whether a change is material, and never decides whether the manager is told.** Code recomputes the score and applies the definition in F6-AC-06. A model shown its own prior answer is reluctant to move; if it also judged materiality that reluctance would compound, and a missed update would be indistinguishable from a genuine no-change. |
| **F6-RS-11** | Availability dropping to zero is a code rule, not a judgement call: it forces the call to surface under the forced-call exception (F6-AC-05) whatever the model would have concluded. An injury is not a matter of opinion. |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **F6-AC-01** | Selected calls survive a refresh and become constraints, not suggestions: their cash and free transfer are already committed and their player is treated as part of the squad. |
| **F6-AC-02** | A selected call reads *selected · locked*, so it is clear why it did not change. |
| **F6-AC-03** | Rejected calls are suppressed for the rest of the gameweek. They return only if the rejected premise has materially changed, and must be labelled as such. |
| **F6-AC-04** | Pending calls are discarded and rewritten freely. |
| **F6-AC-05** | **Exception: a forced call ignores suppression.** If a starter becomes unavailable, that call must surface even if a version of it was rejected earlier. |
| **F6-AC-06** | **"Materially changed" has one definition:** a call is reported when it crosses a conviction band boundary, or when it can no longer be executed. Smaller movements are silent. |
| **F6-AC-07** | One refresh control, in the Assistant status bar (3.1), scoped to the screen it is on and naming that scope on itself — all categories on the overview, one category on a decision tab, the season plan on the Chips tab. |
| **F6-AC-08** | There are no per-category refresh controls on the overview: one rule is easier to trust than a rule plus three shortcuts. |
| **F6-AC-09** | The news-alert token's own refresh (F8) always triggers an all-scope run, because new team news is squad-wide, and a scoped run must never half-clear it. |
| **F6-AC-10** | **Every refresh is confirmed by an interstitial before it runs**, naming its scope, stating the last-run time and whether squad news is outstanding, and explaining the outcome in four lines: what is kept, what is forced back, what is rewritten, what stays out. A scoped run also states which categories are left alone. |
| **F6-AC-11** | **A refresh produces a diff, never a silent replace.** After the run the app reports per call what returned to pending (with the reason in numbers), what resurfaced, what changed band ("was 84%, now 71%"), and a count of untouched calls. |
| **F6-AC-12** | If nothing was invalidated, resurfaced or moved band, no sheet appears. |
| **F6-AC-13** | **Each affected call carries a transient tag on its own card until it has been viewed** — *RETURNED*, *RESURFACED*, *WAS 84%* for a band move, or *NEW* / *UPDATED* from the run itself — beside the call's title, truncating before the title does. Without them the diff is a sheet the manager dismisses and then cannot find his way back to. |
| **F6-AC-14** | The last-run time is always visible, and always reflects the last *successful* run. |
| **F6-AC-15** | Nothing ever refreshes on its own, and a refresh must never fire while the manager is mid-decision. |
| **F6-AC-16** | **The Thinking state is this feature's working state, and every route that re-reads the world passes through it** — the first open after sign-in (F7), a squad correction (F2) and every refresh scope here. |
| **F6-AC-17** | The Thinking state names the process, states the scale of the job in real figures (decisions, players and fixtures considered), and narrates the step in progress citing real values. |
| **F6-AC-18** | The Thinking state shows a pipeline of completed steps with elapsed time, the running step and the queued ones, with exactly one step marked running at any moment and a step's label and state never contradicting each other. |
| **F6-AC-19** | The Thinking state states its expected duration and is cancellable for the whole of it (Performance NFR). |
| **F6-AC-20** | **Cancelling abandons the run and returns to the screen it was launched from with every previous call, decision and the last-run time untouched.** A cancelled run is treated exactly as a run that never started, never as a failed one. |
| **Unhappy Paths** |  |
| **F6-UP-01** | **The generation fails mid-run.** Acceptance: a card over the Assistant, not a dead end or a blank screen. It states the attempt time and that nothing changed, shows which pipeline steps completed and which broke, and offers two ways out — try again, or keep what you have. Dismissing returns to the calls with every decision intact, and the last-run time still reads the last successful run, because a failed run must never age the advice. |
| **F6-UP-02** | **FPL's data feed is unreachable.** Acceptance: distinct from a failed run — the source is gone, so the refresh control reads *off* rather than failing on tap. An amber strip timestamps the whole screen ("showing 19:52 data · 39 minutes old"), and a card states what is frozen (new calls, refresh, chip re-planning) and what is not (the squad, prices, the manager's own decisions), and names the real risk: team news he cannot see. Navigation is never dimmed. |
| **F6-UP-03** | **The gameweek rolls over between sessions.** Acceptance: a new gameweek is a clean slate and the one refresh that keeps nothing. The previous shortlist, decisions, filters and pending calls are all discarded and advice is regenerated from the squad FPL reports at that point. Nothing is carried forward and nothing is replayed. The distinction from a within-gameweek refresh must be stated to the manager, not implied. |
| **F6-UP-04** | **A deadline passes mid-session.** Acceptance: not caught until the next open. An in-session deadline clock and lock is parked, not built. |
